entries.title: I Samuel 16:1
segments:
The Beth-lehemite; so called from his residing in Bethlehem. 
 
No sorrows should ever lead us to murmur at the dealings of God, or to neglect the duties to which he calls us.

entries.title: I Samuel 16:2
segments: When God requires men to engage in perilous services, they need not fear; if they trust in him and follow his directions, he will protect them and give them all desirable success.

entries.title: I Samuel 16:4
segments: Trembled at his coming; perhaps fearing that he had come to rebuke them for some neglect of duty.

entries.title: I Samuel 16:7
segments: As God looks upon the heart, and judges of men according to their real character, the great object of all should be, not outward appearance or external accomplishments merely, but internal purity and the exercise of such feelings as are pleasing to God.

entries.title: I Samuel 16:11
segments:
Sit down; to feast on the sacrifice. 
 
Those who are faithful in the duties of private life, will be most likely to be so in the duties of public life.

entries.title: I Samuel 16:13
segments: The Spirit of the Lord came upon David; to fit him to become king of Israel.

entries.title: I Samuel 16:14
segments:
Departed from Saul; thus he lost the qualifications which God had before given him for the successful discharge of public business. 
 
  An evil spirit from the Lord troubled him; the meaning seems to be that God gave him up the the power of an evil spirit, which from time to time assailed him, filling him with melancholy suspicion and ungovernable anger.

entries.title: I Samuel 16:16
segments: Thou shalt be well; they hoped that music would cheer up his spirits, and remove his difficulties.

entries.title: I Samuel 16:17
segments: Human expedients may for a time lessen one's sorrow; yet there is no permanent relief from the sad effects of sin but in heartily forsaking it, and believing in Jesus Christ, who died, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God.
